findings.text: The root `Action` that called `helpCommand` was removed and replaced by `CommandNotFound`. Running `asdf` with no arguments no longer prints asdf's custom help (`help.Print` with the version and plugin list). urfave/cli's default app help is shown instead, which is a regression.

`CommandNotFound` ignores the error returned by `helpCommand`. `helpCommand` already calls `cli.OsExiter(1)` on its own errors, so with an overridden `OsExiter` the handler can run `OsExiter` twice. The swap from `os.Exit` to the overridable `OsExiter` also means execution now continues after the exit call in the many call sites that have no `return` after it. One example is `installCommand` after the `NoVersionSetError` branch, which goes on to log 'error installing version' and keep installing.

0.reason: The patch removes the root `Action` that called `helpCommand` and only adds `CommandNotFound`, which runs only for unknown subcommands, so running `asdf` with no arguments now falls back to urfave/cli's default help instead of asdf's own `help.Print` output.

1.reason: `cli.OsExiter` defaults to `os.Exit`, so in real runs the process still exits right away; the double-exit and keep-running paths only happen when a test overrides `OsExiter`, so this is not a runtime defect and is unrelated to the env-var leak.
